rows.q: Does influence recovery mean escaping every social influence?

explanationUnit.mainArgument:
Recovery does not mean escaping all influence. Nor does it mean returning to a pure self
untouched by relationship. No life forms itself completely outside shared reality. Language,
emotion, value, identity, and modes of action all develop through long interaction with other
runtimes. What needs to be recovered is not an influence-free self, but the capacity to compare
inherited interpretations with present reality again.

explanationUnit.mainArgument:
Complete release does not require denying the past. It requires recognizing that the shared
runtime has completed the reality it once carried. The experiences created together remain.
Influence remains. Growth remains. But these no longer require the original structure in order to
continue existing. A relationship may end while its influence remains. An organization may
disappear while its knowledge continues. A team may dissolve while its experience enters later
realities.
What ends is the form through which reality was jointly organized—not everything that the
shared reality created. Every shared runtime leaves residue: shared experience, shared memory,
shared capacities, relational patterns, operating habits, and new understandings of reality. These
do not remain sealed in the past. Members carry them into later relationships, teams, families,
organizations, and other shared realities. What one runtime has produced becomes part of the
conditions from which later runtimes begin.

explanationUnit.mainArgument:
This common orientation does not mean that everyone has the same experience. Every life still
carries its own body, history, emotion, position, and interpretation. What changes is that attention,
judgment, expectation, and action increasingly converge upon the same portion of reality.
Different lives may continue to disagree while nevertheless reorganizing themselves around the
same object. This is where Shared Projection begins.

rows.q: Do people need to agree for shared projection to take shape?

explanationUnit.mainArgument:
Shared Projection therefore does not eliminate difference. It depends upon difference remaining
present. During the same national election, people may support opposing positions. In the same
market, one participant may buy an asset, another may sell it, and another may remain outside
the market entirely. Faced with the same technology, some people may be hopeful, others
skeptical, and others resistant. Their interpretations may diverge sharply, but all of them are
nevertheless adjusting themselves in relation to the same reality. What was once an event
experienced locally begins to become something to which an entire collective must respond.

explanationUnit.mainArgument:
What ends, therefore, is not necessarily every connection between the people involved. What ends
is a particular way of jointly organizing reality.
 
Members may continue respecting one another, remembering one another, or maintaining contact.
What has changed is that they no longer organize themselves around the same responsibilities,
goals, and reality. The runtime releases positions that once had to be maintained together: roles,
boundaries, resources, and expectations gradually return to other structures. Each runtime re-
enters reality from a new position.
